candidates.source_body_excerpt: Staff at 10 primary schools have been equipped to inspire the next generation of engineers. Last week, staff from the schools across Rochdale and Oldham took part in a CPD training day so they could the deliver the Primary Engineer Vehicle Programme in their schools. The programme allows pupils to build and test their own vehicle models while getting to interact with engineering professionals in class, as well as attending a joint school event as they celebrate their achievements at the end of the programme. The practical session gave teachers a hands-on opportunity to build their confidence in delivering STEM projects to pupils. The current academic year marks first year of partnership between Rochdale Council, Rochdale Development and Primary Engineers with the aim of inspiring Rochdale’s next generation of engineers. READ MORE: Care home plan approved despite objections The vehicle programme gives the opportunity for schools to gain access to a full package of opportunities, including a full day CPD training course, high-quality kits and classroom resources which will enable 60 pupils in each school to build 15 shoebox locomotives and 15 motorised locomotives. The schools will also receive all resources to continue the programme with new pupils in their school for the next academic year.

candidates.source_summary: Plans to turn a family home into a residential care home for adults have been approved despite more than 20 objections.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to turn a family home into a residential care home for adults have been approved despite more than 20 objections. Saf Khaliq applied to Rochdale Council to turn 9 Thornham New Road, Castleton, into an eight-bedroom residential home to care for up to eight adults. There will be two staff on the premises at all times. Among the objections, concerns were raised about parking already being an issue in Thornham New Road. Objections were also raised that the plan is unsustainable and is an over intensification of a single family home and it would out of character for the area. There were also concerns about noise and general disturbance. The council’s highways department raised no objection to the plan, adding that the site is located on an established residential road with good access to the wider highway network and public transport. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Six people have been arrested in Middleton for attempting to import cannabis worth almost £6 million from Canada. Police in Canada uncovered the plan and officers there swapped the cannabis — which was hidden with a shipment of timber — for a synthetic product. GMP said: “Through the strong working relationship developed between our SOCG officers and Canadian law enforcement partners, we were alerted to an attempted import of approximately 590kg of cannabis, which was concealed within a large lumber shipment destined for the UK. “The drugs, worth an estimated street value of £5.9 million, had been hidden within sophisticated concealments inside the shipment. “Canadian authorities successfully seized the cannabis before it left the country, and replaced it with a synthetic substitute. “Following its arrival at docks in Liverpool, we closely monitored the container as it was transported by HGV to an address in Heywood Old Road in Middleton. “Officers maintained surveillance on the shipment and observed a number of individuals interacting with the container.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A man who played a significant role in an organised crime group which supplied class A drugs across Rochdale has been jailed for 10 years and six months. An investigation into Haider Ali was launched following information received that a drug deal had taken place from a car parked in Baron Street, in Rochdale town centre, just before midnight on January 4, 2025. Officers began to follow the vehicle and when it came to a stop at a local petrol station, officers immediately executed a reinforced stop to prevent it from making off. Ali, who was travelling as a passenger, exited the vehicle and began to speedily walk away before officers detained him. Following searches, Ali was found to be in possession of more than £1,000 in cash, and two mobile phones, all of which were seized. Ali was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of class A drugs and taken to custody where further searches recovered two bundles of several wraps of a brown and a white substance. Tests later confirmed these substances to be heroin and cocaine. A pre-paid mobile phone seized from Ali was confirmed to be the Adam drug line. Following this, investigators also uncovered that Ali was not only dealing drugs at street level, but he was also managing other street dealers. Evidence suggested that Ali had progressed from being a street dealer in 2014 to holding a significant role within the Adam OCG in 2024 into 2025, managing street dealers and the dedicated dealer phone, and directing those below him on where there next deal is.

candidates.source_summary: An increase in absences caused by stress and depression has contributed to more than 30,000 sick days among Rochdale Council staff — and more than £4.2 million in sick pay.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: An increase in absences caused by stress and depression has contributed to more than 30,000 sick days among Rochdale Council staff — and more than £4.2 million in sick pay. Next week, the council’s Employment and Equalities Committee will consider the steps being taken to support staff after figures for 2025-26 show total number of days lost was 30,707.80, which equates to £4,237,676.40 in sick pay. This averages 11.49 days per full-time employee due to sickness absence, with the main reason being stress/depression — an 11.2% increase on the previous year’s total of 10.33 days. The latest figures show that 65% were long-term absences, 35% were short-term absences and both are consistent with figures for previous years. The report says that the council is continuing to support staff with their health and wellbeing, and is providing a programme of initiatives throughout the year. This includes prevention of ill health and promotion of staff wellbeing. Detailed analysis of the 2025/2026 figures show that the main reasons for long-term absence were stress/depression, operative/post-operative and back and sprains, strains, bruises and breaks. For short-term absences, the reasons are stress/depression, colds/flu/viral infections, diarrhoea/ vomiting/sickness bug.

Ignite, sponsored by car supermarket The Trade Centre UK and organised by Rochdale Development Agency, transformed the square and gardens around the town hall into a trail of fire, lights and entertainment. The multi-sensory experience was the most ambitious fire and light installation yet from outdoor arts specialists Walk the Plank, and Ignite was its north-west premiere. Visitors were taken on a dramatic journey as they walked through the glowing embers of human metabolism – the silent furnace that keeps us alive, continuously generating heat to power all the body’s functions. candidates.source_summary: Campaigners fighting to save Rochdale's College Bank flats from demolition are calling on community leaders to step in and save the landmark tower blocks
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Campaigners fighting to save Rochdale’s College Bank flats from demolition are calling on community leaders to step in and save the landmark tower blocks. Yesterday, Rochdale Boroughwide Housing announced that demolition and redevelopment of the site is the only viable option for the 61-year-old tower blocks known as the Seven Sisters. It said refurbishing them would cost at least £269 million and take up to 12 years — estimated at £388,000 for each of the 766 flats before VAT. RBH said the renovations would add another 50 years to the lifespan of the buildings, while redevelopment would provide 601 homes in a mix of sizes, creating a minimum additional 249 bedrooms, and the properties would last “significantly longer”. Reacting to the news, Greater Manchester Tenants Union said the decision was part of a “managed decline” overseen by the housing provider — a claim RBH denies. GMTU said: “Campaigners and the wider community are very disappointed with the decision to pursue demolition by RBH. “For 10 years the tenants and leaseholders of College Bank have suffered one mistaken decision after another. “RBH claims the decision is based upon ‘a detailed review of all available scenarios’ but it has only allowed for a costing of an overpriced refurbishment plan based upon installing a second staircase in each block of College Bank (under new regulations following the Grenfell disaster).”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: John Morris has long campaigned for a study into the health impacts of Britain's nuclear programme A nuclear test veteran who developed cancer and lost his four-month-old son, has said hearing an independent panel will look into Britain's atomic programme was "a magical moment". John Morris, from Rochdale, was sent to Christmas Island in the 1950s to work on the UK's growing nuclear programme - and now believes the loss of his son was due to radiation exposure picked up on the island. Morris, who alongside fellow veterans have long campaigned for an investigation, said this announcement feels different "without a shadow of a doubt". Burnham told campaigners in Downing Street that he would launch an independent investigation Morris said he was 18 when he was sent to Christmas Island, in the Pacific Ocean, to work as a laundry operator on a British nuclear site.

candidates.source_summary: The Challenge Cup will enter an exciting new era in 2027, with a refreshed format, a bold new identity and a renewed ambition to make one of rugby league's most iconic competitions bigger, more compelling and more accessible to fans.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The 2027 Challenge Cup campaign will kick off on the weekend of January 16-17, bringing together clubs from across the rugby league pyramid in a format that celebrates the depth and heritage of the sport, while building towards the ultimate prize at Wembley Stadium. The first round draw will take place on Monday 30 November at Wembley Stadium, live on the newly-launched Challenge Cup YouTube channel. It will feature 28 community clubs, offering teams from across the country a chance to face the professional game's biggest names on the road to the national stadium. A brand-new identity for the Challenge Cup will be unveiled on Monday, signalling the beginning of the competition’s next chapter and providing a distinctive platform to connect with existing supporters, attract new audiences and elevate the competition's profile. The launch will also include the announcement of a new commercial partner and a dedicated ticket sales window, giving rugby league fans an exclusive opportunity to secure their place at Wembley Stadium on Saturday 5 June. Under the revised format, the bottom four Super League teams from 2026, plus newly-promoted London Broncos, will enter in the fourth round, with the remaining top-flight clubs, excluding Catalans Dragons and Toulouse Olympique (who will not participate in 2027), joining in the fifth round. The Challenge Cup will once again start in January with a full round of community club ties, before 10 Championship clubs join in the second round, the remaining 10 joining in the third round. The fourth and fifth rounds will take place in March, followed by the quarter-finals in April and the semi-finals on the weekend of May 8-9. The successful finalists will then have four weeks to prepare for the Challenge Cup Final on Saturday 5 June. The Women's Challenge Cup final will once again take centre stage at Wembley on Saturday 5 June as part of Finals Day, celebrating the continued growth and importance of the women's game. The Wheelchair Challenge Cup final will follow, on the weekend of June 26-27, ensuring the competition's revitalised chapter embraces all forms of the sport.

candidates.source_summary: The Championship is set for a new-look 2027 season, with an East and West Conference format, an expanded race for the play-offs and a fresh approach to the 1895 Cup.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Under the improved structure, clubs will play 18 league fixtures within their own conference, with nine home games and nine away games, before the top five in each conference progress to the Championship play-offs. A four-week play-off series will build towards a Grand Final scheduled for October 3, while the Shield Trophy will offer a further opportunity for clubs outside the leading places to compete for silverware. The conference model will give clubs a clear route through the regular season, with all 18 league fixtures played against opponents from their own conference. Each club will have nine opportunities to play in front of their home supporters, alongside nine away fixtures, with conference standings determining qualification for the Championship play-offs. The opening conference round is scheduled for January 21–24, with the final round of league fixtures planned for September 2–5. Week 1: The top five teams in both the East and West conferences will reach the play-offs. In week one, fourth will play fifth in each conference for a place in the next round. Week 2: In week two, the team that finished top of each conference will play the lowest-placed team still in the competition from that conference. The teams that finished second and third will also play each other within their own conference. Week 3: The winners of those games will meet in the East and West Conference Finals in week three. In each final, the team that finished higher in the league will play at home.

candidates.source_summary: Living Well Rochdale has carried out 2,000 free community health checks across Rochdale, Heywood and Middleton. The team referred 1,017 people to their GP for further assessment.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Living Well Rochdale has carried out 2,000 free community health checks across Rochdale, Heywood and Middleton. The team referred 1,017 people to their GP for further assessment. Rochdale Borough Council commissioned the programme, which launched on 31 October 2025. Living Well Rochdale’s cardiovascular disease team has held sessions at community venues, GP practices, workplaces, places of worship and cash and carry stores. The checks include blood pressure, height and weight measurements and a finger-prick blood test for blood sugar and cholesterol. Participants are also given their body mass index and a QRISK3 score, which estimates their risk of cardiovascular disease over the next 10 years. Kuiama Thompson, director of public health and communities at Rochdale Borough Council, said, “This is another milestone in a successful collaboration between the council and Living Well in tackling cardiovascular disease in our borough. “We're very proud of the innovative approach that we've developed with Living Well, which addresses health inequalities by understanding and putting the needs of our residents first. “This is a model of bringing healthcare into communities, in turn saving lives across the borough. By making those vital early interventions with these health checks we can reduce cardiovascular disease and ensure that all of our residents are given the chance they deserve to live longer and healthier lives.” Living Well Rochdale and the council’s public health team were highly commended in the Community Engagement category at the 2026 MJ Awards. candidates.source_summary: A document has been approved by town hall chiefs
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A plan that will shape the future of Rochdale has been signed off and sent to the government for approval. The borough’s Local Plan will mould how it will look and its priorities until 2039. Under the plans, around 11,000 new homes will be built and the borough’s railway stations will get a major revamp. After one final round of consultation, the hefty 175-page document has been approved by town hall chiefs. Once given the green light by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, it is expected that formal adoption of the plan will come later in 2027 or early 2028. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter The main controversy of the Local Plan had been reducing the minimum threshold of affordable housing from 20 per cent to 15 pc. This was done because it was not financially viable, a town hall meeting in July was told. But the latest town hall meeting saw the cabinet put that threshold back up to 20 pc for ‘all developments of 10 dwellings or more’. Housing forms a substantial part of the plan, with the land carved out for new homes already mapped out by the Places for Everyone plan. The PfE plan is a giant housing strategy adopted by nine out of 10 Greater Manchester councils. PfE would see around 175,000 homes built across the city region over the next two decades and is expected to bring forward investment and major redevelopment in Rochdale and across the city-region. The Rochdale council is anticipating a major boost in the coming years through the Atom Valley scheme. The vision to build 7,000 new homes, create 20,000 ‘high-quality’ jobs and carve out 17m sq ft of employment land has already taken hold. But the Local Plan is focusing on Rochdale alone. The Rochdale Rail Corridor Strategy is at the beating heart of what the local authority really wants to achieve. The concept would see the land around transport hubs along the Manchester to Leeds railway line reconfigured into places for people to live, work and play. These hubs would focus on the stations in Rochdale, Castleton, Mills Hill, Smithy Bridge, Littleborough and a new Slattocks station. To get the very latest Greater Manchester stories in your newsfeed - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source Combined with walking and cycling routes, park and rides, new public realms and community spaces, these hubs hope to attract more people into the area and in turn boost the local economy. Overall, the strategic plan covered a huge array of topics that would influence how the borough would grow. These areas include climate and energy, economic growth and town centres, housing, natural environment, design and place-making, healthy communities and sustainable transport. All these categories have been considered for each town and local centre across the area, which have been prioritised in order of importance to the borough’s growth ambitions.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A pioneering football-based project is helping young girls in the borough build confidence, friendships and resilience through the power of sport. Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust and Pennine Care Charity have teamed up with Rochdale AFC Community Trust to deliver a new programme for girls aged six to 11 who are waiting for, or already receiving, support from Rochdale child and adolescent mental health services (CAMHS). The free 36-week pilot uses fun football activities to help girls stay active and develop their confidence, social skills and emotional wellbeing in a safe and welcoming environment. The programme was developed following feedback from parents of children receiving support from CAMHS, who highlighted the need for activities to help their children build self-esteem and make friends. The project is funded by the Football Association’s Empower Her Fund, which supports opportunities for women and girls to get involved in football. Sessions are delivered by experienced staff from Rochdale AFC Community Trust. Sixteen girls have taken part so far, with early feedback showing how much they are enjoying the sessions and the opportunities to build confidence and make new friends. Anders Cox, clinical lead at Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale CAMHS, run by Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust, said: “Getting active, making friends and feeling part of something can all support young people’s mental health. “This project gives the girls a fun and welcoming environment where they can build their confidence, learn new skills and enjoy being active together.”
